strengths: Clear problem formulation with comprehensive review of 6 baseline methods and detailed characterization of their limitations (Table 1)
Elegant directional reparameterization technique (Eq. 8) that maintains geometric consistency with nearest-neighbor operation while enabling gradient flow
Novel SF-DiVeQ extension addressing codebook collapse without replacement heuristics, with compelling evidence of superior codebook-latent alignment (Fig. 4)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 5 datasets, multiple metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, FID), 6 baselines, extensive ablations (batch size, learning rate, variance), and Residual VQ generalization tests
Insightful analysis identifying codebook misalignment as previously unrecognized failure mode in existing methods, with theoretical connection to rate-distortion violations
Strong reproducibility: detailed implementation specifications, 3-run averaging, drop-in replacement design requiring minimal code changes
Consistent improvements across VQ-VAE compression task (5-10% LPIPS reduction) and multiple datasets (CELEBA-HQ, FFHQ, AFHQ, LSUN variants)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution is incremental modification of NSVQ (Eq. 7), replacing random noise with directional noise vd = v + (ci* - z), representing modest conceptual advance
Contradicts 'no hyperparameter tuning' claim: σ² requires task-specific setting (10⁻³ for VQ-VAE, 10⁻² for VQGAN), with Fig. 20-21 showing performance sensitivity to this choice

Lacks theoretical rigor: no formal error bounds for directional reparameterization, SF-DiVeQ's misalignment prevention relies on intuition rather than rigorous analysis, connection to rate-distortion theory feels post-hoc
VQGAN generation results inconsistent: Table 2 shows non-monotonic FID with increasing bitrate; NSVQ's catastrophic performance (81.5 FID at bitrate 8) raises baseline implementation concerns

SF-DiVeQ initialization overhead contradicts simplicity claims: requires skipping VQ for initial epochs, careful averaging of recent latents (20-50 iterations), and continuous codebook usage tracking (Appendix A.5)

Comparison fairness concerns: proposed codebook replacement differs from baselines (importance sampling vs. random), RT required extensive tuning across decay rates, unclear if implementation gaps exist across methods
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests despite averaging over 3 runs; some improvements appear within potential noise margins
Marginal quantitative gains in many scenarios: ~10-15% LPIPS improvement, minimal gains at higher bitrates, unclear practical benefit justifying added complexity

Presentation issues: critical insights scattered across 36-page paper with appendices, circular logic in misalignment analysis (Sec. 4, C.6), lack of design justifications (e.g., stop gradient placement)

Incomplete coverage: FSQ/RPQ/BSQ/LFQ omitted from comparisons, no computational cost analysis, missing guidance on when to use DiVeQ vs. SF-DiVeQ, limited discussion of post-2022 relevance as diffusion models gain dominance
